# Contact-state and restoration observations

`contact_state.tsv` records actual unchanged Java survive, inhibited, frozen, paralyzed, neutralized, and segmentsRestoreEffects calls.
Source twice and the bundled JAR produced identical bytes.
The four compiled helper classes also match across both backends.
The fixture contains 94 cases, 218 snapshots, 654 actor views, and 124 actual calls.
Every actor view contains all 154 original organism observations.
Every snapshot includes genotype references, ten world values, 52 statistics fields, 49 getters, and the following RNG suffix.

## Comparison contract

The contract and fixed ledger were declared before Rust comparison.
Compare scalar, effect, photo, gas, statistics, velocity, endpoint, bounds, ARGB, reaction, identity, ordering, and RNG observations exactly.
Only organism geometry fields `_m`, `_m1`, `_m2`, `_mass`, and `_I` retain the existing geometry allowance.
For finite geometry, use `1e-10 * max(1, abs(expected))`.
Check geometric NaN classification and signed infinity explicitly.
No other floating tolerance or NaN substitution applies.

Actual GeneticCode identity connects primary, infected, saved, and statistics holders to `g0` through `g4`.
Full G/N blocks preserve every actual genome and gene value.
Per-Gene mutable-object alias topology remains covered by the separate genetics fixture.
Only `_world` and `_visibleWorld` are named O collaborator exclusions.
Setup selection is separate source callback-routing metadata.
No other source observations receive an unsupported-state disposition.

## Execution and constructor authority

Compile `tools/reference/ContactStateOracle.java` against each pinned backend.
Run `biogenesis.ContactStateOracle NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` with the isolated profile arguments recorded in provenance.
The helper validates all four explicit profile roots through `toRealPath` before simulation access.
It rejects existing output directories and writes its new file with `CREATE_NEW`.
Six actual negative invocations cover every omitted root, an escaped profile symlink, and existing output preservation.
The existing runner bounds positive processes to 120 seconds and negative processes to 30 seconds.
It cleans each owned process group afterward.

Each case resets actual source defaults and records all 147 mutable primitive settings.
Initial organism attempts are zero; initial oxygen is `1000`.
Mutation bounds are `0..10000`; meta mutation is zero.
GREEN selection weight is seven; other selectable weights are zero.
The setup seed is `827364`.
Explicit settings supply payment costs, selected effect parameters, and larger world dimensions where needed.
No genesis or complete world frame runs.

Five original genomes receive stable identities.
`g0` is explicit and supplies the victim; `g1` and `g2` are explicit one-GREEN-gene actor codes.
`g3` and `g4` use actual GeneticCode.clone on `g0`.
Their recipes and all supplied values appear in `input` G/N blocks before actor creation.
Ordinary genes have length `12`, theta `index * 0.25`, branch `0`, and default reactions.
Symmetry, mirror, spore modifier, passive mode, modified sky, colors, and lengths are explicit construction inputs.
All other constructor modifiers retain the recorded defaults.
Generation is `41`; clade is `root`.

The helper creates actual headless VisibleWorld and World objects.
It uses actual gas-add, paste, and World.addOrganism methods.
Original actor order is peer, victim, then killer, with initial IDs `0,1,2`.
Peer is selected before the first add.
Ordinary positions are peer `(1000,1000)`, victim `(3500,3500)`, and killer `(2000,2000)`.
The selected peer avoids MainWindow callbacks without mocks.
All creation, population, gas, identity, storage, and statistics effects remain actual source behavior.

Large numeric cases use `1000000000` by `1000000000` worlds and a victim centered at `(500000000,500000000)`.
Their large positive genes are genuinely constructed and pasted successfully.
They do not rely on malformed geometry or an uninitialized actor.
The complete large-world geometry and numeric state remain observed.

## Labelled state inputs

Each first snapshot follows recorded setup controls.
The common baseline supplies victim energy `20` and actor energy `1000`.
It supplies victim healing `10`, antiviral `0`, gold `0`, and spore version `1`.
Plant, consumer, fungus, coral, injury, frozen, extra-effects, and only-C4 flags are explicitly controlled.
Movement, reaction, frame movement, can-dodge, and dodge flags begin true unless overridden.
Body update-effects begins zero.
Victim temporary color is MAGENTA with seven frames; killer temporary color is RED with five frames.
Photo coefficients begin at the supplied `index + 0.25` values.
Victim infection and saved references initially hold `g3` and `g4`.

Phenotype Color[] controls preserve valid constructed body lengths.
They allow direct observation of each current-color branch without inventing contact eligibility or transformation history.
The six palette cases each supply all 46 base colors, 18 internal colors, an unknown ARGB, and translucent MAGENTA.
Opaque and translucent colors remain distinct full-ARGB values.

Actor classification controls describe inputs to the actual helper methods.
They do not claim that a physical contact matrix would select every supplied actor/body combination.
Negative, NaN, and infinite scalar controls are explicit method-level observations on real placed actors.
They do not claim that the player UI accepts those values.
No null primary genotype, null phenotype color, raw allocation, or fake collaborator is needed.

## Covered outcomes

| Group | Actual source observations |
| --- | --- |
| Palette | Every base/internal current color, unknown ARGB, and full-ARGB distinction across all six methods. |
| Survival | Healing reset, exact MAGENTA conversion, unchanged translucent color, and unconditional gray actor tint. |
| Inhibition | Spore-version gate, plant/other damage colors, per-segment payments, and mandatory later restoration. |
| Full freezing | Every color group, sky/passive modifiers, original DARKGREEN gene identity, jade delay wrapping, and photo differences. |
| Paralysis | Teal/cyan processing and retained full-freeze caches for unrelated colors. |
| Neutralization | Plant/consumer/coral damage, pure immunity, classified actors, healing/plague gates, gold-update gates, and delayed injury/tint. |
| Payments | Zero costs, full/partial/empty oxygen, insufficient energy, negative oxygen, NaN/infinity, and self versus distinct payers. |
| Cache state | Explicit reset versus retention, pure auburn retention, modified sky restoration, and eye cache retention through freezing. |
| Restoration modifiers | Passive/nonpassive teal, symmetry-three mirrors, symmetry eight, and spore boundaries `2,3,6,7`. |
| Dodge | Classification guards, sky/infection guards, passive bypass, methane/plant restrictions, and retained can-dodge without can-react. |
| Reproduction | Plant/consumer/fungus/transferring-virus/spore minima, integer overflow, and implicit float rounding. |
| Ordered sequences | Survival before neutralization, repeated restoration after inhibition, and restoration after full freezing. |

Payments occur in ascending segment order for the five contact-state methods.
Partial respiration can consume energy and oxygen while returning false and leaving the relevant phenotype unchanged.
Other segments continue through their later attempts.
No helper invents a death event when a payer reaches or crosses an energy boundary.
Survival has no payment and always tints its actor.

Inhibition always invokes the real restoration method afterward, including cases without successful damage.
Freezing and paralysis retain their different flag-reset scopes.
Bark can become frozen without setting injury; winter-type conversions retain their separate update/photo behavior.
Mint damage does not clear infection or saved-code references.
Its tint and injury flag follow the completed source loop.
Negative antiviral counts remain nonzero immunity inputs.

Restoration processes segments in descending order.
The reverse-FLOWER overflow case observes a final late value of `1` after a genuine overflowing sequence.
Symmetry-three fertility preserves integer `5/6` and `2/3` coefficients.
The corresponding immune/healing coefficients preserve integer `50/6` and `20/3` divisions.
Restoration does not recreate initial organism effects or rebuild cached body coordinates.

The large BLOND restoration observes early energy `1932735279`.
The large ordinary FLOWER case observes late value `214748352`.
The infectious FLOWER case observes late value `16777220` and reproduction energy `3019942`.
Those values come from actual Java calls, including the integer-division/implicit-float Math.round overload.
The large GOLD case observes maximum age `-474` through double rounding and narrowing long-to-int conversion.
The paired GOLD divisors distinguish exact-half rounding from the next larger divisor.
Wrapped BLOND/GOLD totals retain their actual negative results and conditional cache behavior.

All 218 recorded following RNG suffixes are identical.
The methods consume no additional source RNG in these observations.
The helper peeks through serialized Random copies without advancing the live stream.

## TSV protocol

The fixture reuses the death/infection `C/U/I/A/P/K/O/H/W/S/T/G/N/R/E` grammar.
Rows are tab-separated ASCII with a final newline.
Doubles use sixteen raw IEEE hexadecimal digits.
Arrays retain comma-separated order; nullable references use `~`.
GeneticCode O fields record presence; H records actual identities.
Handle Organism identity before Rectangle values because Organism extends Rectangle.

`K` columns are stage, exact operation, victim role, and actor argument.
Operations are `survive`, `inhibited`, `frozen`, `paralyzed`, `neutralized`, and `segmentsRestoreEffects`.
Actor arguments are `killer` or `self`; restoration uses `~`.
The target is always `victim`.

I targets retain the existing actor, world, statistics, and genome forms.
`actor:victim:_mphoto` supplies a `double[]`.
`genome:g0:gene0._color` invokes the real source gene setter with a supplied full-ARGB Color.
The helper supports labelled gene length setters, but no such setter appears in this final fixture.
Large lengths are construction inputs instead.
All source input targets and types are recorded in the provenance.
No V/Q/J rows, newborn discovery, candidate disposition, or extra source-only actor state is required.

Calls comprise four survive, ten inhibited, 32 frozen, seven paralyzed, 23 neutralized, and 48 restoration operations.
No diagnostic or rejected-state rows are silently excluded.
No post-call observation becomes a constructor input.

Source methods occupy `Organism.java:5231-5603`; restoration occupies `Organism.java:916-1167`.
Source useEnergy occupies `Organism.java:4588-4597`; tint behavior occupies `Organism.java:19320-19323`.
The provenance records source/backend/helper hashes, exact commands, versions, equality, guards, and the unchanged production pin.
All 74 original files and all 23 earlier TSV fixtures retain their recorded hashes.
The first 91-case source/source/JAR run remains preserved.
Those 91 cases remain byte-identical in the final 94-case fixture.

These observations do not establish physical contact eligibility, full color-matrix integration, a complete frame, UI, or persistence compatibility.
They do not enumerate every combination of unrelated cached flags.
Rust comparison and integration results remain separate from this Java observation provenance.
